verdict.line: You lose this if you walk into his 625-range Q poke with your E on cooldown and no way to close distance; you win it if you catch his W (Remove Scurvy) on cooldown and land the full E into W stun chain.

brief.thesis: Gangplank out-ranges you by nearly 200 units with Q (Parrrley, 625 range, 5s cooldown) while your only gap-closer is E (Slice and Dice, 450 range), so every trade starts with him choosing to poke or not. His W (Remove Scurvy) also clears any crowd control on him, so your W (Ruthless Predator) stun only matters as a kill tool when his W is already down — otherwise he just cleanses and heals off the damage.

theirWindow.what: You have no way to close the gap, so he free-hits you with Q and stacks his passive poison with autos. Hold position at max wave range and eat the poke rather than walking up to trade.

yourWindow.when: his W (Remove Scurvy, 22-18s cd) is down
yourWindow.what: Commit the full combo: E into him, then W for the stun (3 hits and a 1.5s stun if you're above 50 Fury), then Q. He can't cleanse the stun or heal through it, so this is your real kill window, not a random level-up all-in.

powerCurve.note: Q poke range beats your melee kit
W unlocks the E-W-Q stun combo
R adds damage, his W still cleanses
poison stacking and R zoning scale past you

start.why: Measured at 47.4% over 1380 games and the majority pick (56.1%) in this matchup — the regen and damage reduction on the first few autos directly offsets his passive poison chip and Q poke while you're stuck walking up.

boots.why: 87% pick rate and the standard choice here; the flat auto-attack damage reduction cuts into both his on-hit poison and his Q poke, which are the two things actually hurting you before you can engage.

core.why: Opening item on the highest-performing path (51.3% over 230 games) — the shield absorbs a Q poke or two during your approach and the burst passive rewards landing your full stun combo.
Stacks armor shred on top of your empowered E's own armor reduction, which matters because you need every point of burst you can get during the narrow window his W is down.
Completes the 51.3% win-rate path; the damage-over-time conversion and healing let you survive the chip poison and poke damage you eat every time you don't have a kill window.

situational.when: you're ahead and need to survive being focused by his Cannon Barrage or a jungler diving alongside his poke
you're snowballing and want W and E back faster so you get more cracks at his W cooldown window per minute
their jungler or mid adds extra hard crowd control on top of his poke, making the tenacity worth more than the armor

runes.keystoneWhy: The ramping adaptive damage and healing matter specifically because his W (Remove Scurvy) heals him back after trades — Conqueror lets you out-sustain that heal over an extended fight instead of relying on a single burst window to win lane.

summoners.why: The standard pick at 83.3% pick rate and 47.7% win rate — Ignite punishes the all-in window when his W is down and he can't heal off the burn, since Remove Scurvy clears CC but not damage-over-time. Flash+Teleport (43.9% win, 13.7% pick) is the alternative if you need to answer his Cannon Barrage's global map pressure.

playing.title: All-in only when his W is down
playing.detail: Track Remove Scurvy's 22-18s cooldown. Outside that window your stun gets cleansed and healed through; inside it, your W actually kills.

playing.title: Hold range when your E is down
playing.detail: Your longest reach is E at 450; his Q hits from 625. Without E up you cannot close the gap, so don't walk forward and eat free poke.

playing.title: Bank Fury before committing
playing.detail: Above 50 Fury your Q deals and heals more, and your W gets a third hit, destroys shields, and stuns for 1.5s instead of 0.75s. Land a few autos first so the combo lands at full strength.

playing.title: Look for level 3 tempo
playing.detail: Per the common skill order you have Q and E by level 2 but no stun until W at level 3. The moment you hit 3, check if he's extended on CS and punish with the full combo.

playing.title: Use R to win extended fights
playing.detail: Dominus (120/100/80/80/80s cooldown) adds sustained AoE damage and periodic Fury gain from level 6 on — lean on it to outlast his Remove Scurvy sustain in longer trades rather than trying to one-shot him.

playing.title: Contest his Powder Kegs
playing.detail: OP.GG's own read on this matchup is to contest his keg plays directly rather than cede them, since uncontested kegs are free poke damage he gets without ever entering stun range.

playing.title: Stop forcing fights past level 12
playing.detail: His passive poison stacking and Cannon Barrage zoning scale harder than your kit late. Bank your advantage from the levels-3-11 window into plates and objectives rather than looking for a late pick.

brief.patchCaveat: Win rates, build paths, runes, and summoner spells above are measured OP.GG data from live games on the current patch (16.19.1); the timing windows, Fury thresholds, and trade-pattern reasoning are my own read of the ability kits, not OP.GG's.

stats.opponentTip: Be careful of being hit with Gangplank’s Grasp of the Undying + (Q) combo. Focus on contesting Powder Kegs while fighting him. Purchase Executioner’s Calling for a slight edge.
